title: Chapter 14 Quiz — Type Systems & Data Validation

questions.question: The function `def double(x: int) -> int: return x * 2` is called as `double("ab")`. What happens?

options.text: A TypeError is raised at the call, and mypy reports nothing.
It prints 4, because the string is converted to an int first.
It prints abab, and mypy reports nothing, because the function is annotated.
It prints abab, and mypy reports an incompatible argument type for "ab".

questions.explanation: Annotations are stored, not enforced. CPython runs x * 2 on the string and returns abab. Mypy reads the annotation and reports Argument 1 to "double" has incompatible type "str"; expected "int". Lesson 14.1.

questions.question: A file contains `def total(prices):` with `x: int = "3"` in its body and `return sum(prices) + x`. What does default mypy report, with no flags?

options.text: Success, with a note that the bodies of untyped functions are not checked by default.
An assignment error on the line with x: int = "3".
A missing-annotation error for total.
Success with no note, because annotations are optional in Python.

questions.explanation: Default mypy skips the body of a function with no annotations and prints an annotation-unchecked note. --check-untyped-defs reports the assignment error on line 2. --strict adds the no-untyped-def error. Lesson 14.1.

questions.question: Which body makes mypy --strict report success for `def shout(name: str | None) -> str:`?

options.text: return name.upper()
return name.upper() or ""
if name is None: return "", then return name.upper()
return name.lower().upper()

questions.explanation: The None guard narrows name to str on the path that reaches .upper(). The other three still call .upper() on a value that may be None, so mypy reports union-attr. Lesson 14.1.

questions.question: Mypy rejects `def larger(x: T, y: T) -> T: return x if x > y else y` with an unbounded T. Why?

options.text: Because > is not defined for int.
Because an unbounded T promises no methods, so the checker cannot verify x > y. Binding T to a Protocol that declares __gt__ fixes it.
Because a TypeVar must always be bound to a class, not to a Protocol.
Because the return type must be Any when two arguments are compared.

questions.explanation: At run time larger(1, 2) prints 2. The error exists only in the checker's view: mypy reports Unsupported left operand type for > ("T"). Lesson 14.2.

questions.question: A runtime-checkable Protocol `Closable` declares `close(self) -> None`. A class `WrongParams` defines `close(self, force: bool) -> None`. What does `isinstance(WrongParams(), Closable)` return?

options.text: False, because the signatures differ.
TypeError, because the Protocol has a method member.
None, because close returns None.
True, because runtime_checkable checks only that a close attribute exists.

questions.explanation: isinstance on a runtime-checkable Protocol checks attribute names, not signatures, so it prints True. Mypy reports the conflict in the signature. Lesson 14.2.

questions.question: `def total(xs: list[float]) -> float` is called with `ints: list[int] = [1, 2]`. Why is the call rejected, and which annotation fixes it without changing the body?

options.text: int is not a subclass of float in Python, so convert the list with float() first.
The return type must be int when the input is int, so change the return annotation.
list is invariant: the function could append a float to the caller's list. Annotating xs as Sequence[float] fixes it.
Mypy does not check list arguments, so add a runtime isinstance check instead.

questions.explanation: A list[int] is not a list[float] because list is invariant. Sequence is read-only and covariant, so a list[int] is accepted by Sequence[float]; mypy --strict reports no issues on that version. Lesson 14.2.

questions.question: In Pydantic V2, what does `TypeAdapter(int).validate_python(" 7 ")` return, and what does `TypeAdapter(int).validate_python("1", strict=True)` raise?

options.text: 7, and an int_type error.
7, and a float_parsing error.
" 7 " unchanged, with no error.
7, with no error.

questions.explanation: Lax mode (the default) strips the spaces and converts the string to 7. Strict mode accepts only an int, so the string "1" fails with int_type. Lesson 14.3.

questions.question: What does `class Sample(BaseModel): note: Optional[str]` followed by `Sample()` raise?

options.text: Nothing; note is set to None.
A TypeError, because Optional fields cannot be omitted.
A ValidationError whose error type is missing.
A ValidationError whose error type is string_type.

questions.explanation: In Pydantic V2, Optional[str] with no default is required: the field may hold None but must be supplied. The fix is note: Optional[str] = None. Lesson 14.3.

questions.question: Mypy reports "Success: no issues found" for `def average(xs: list[float]) -> float: return sum(xs) / len(xs)`. What does `average([])` do?

options.text: Returns 0.0.
Mypy reports an error at the call site.
Returns nan.
Raises ZeroDivisionError.

questions.explanation: Mypy checks types, not values, so an empty list passes. sum([]) / len([]) divides 0 by 0 at run time and raises ZeroDivisionError. Lesson 14.1.
